title: API key is hard-coded in a script the browser downloads
evidence: api.js is loaded by index.html:25 as a plain <script>. Lines 6 and 11 send the key as a Bearer token from the browser. Anyone who opens the page source or the network tab gets a key that authorises refunds. README.md:6 says the opposite.
failing_case: Open the page, view api.js, copy API_KEY, then POST https://api.orderdesk.test/v1/refunds with that Authorization header. Any visitor can refund any order.
remediation: Move the key to a server. The browser calls a same-site backend that holds the key, checks the user's permissions and forwards the request. Rotate the shipped key.

title: Customer name from the API is written into innerHTML unescaped
evidence: app.js:32 builds the row from a template string and assigns it with innerHTML +=. o.customer.name and o.id (the data-id attribute in the same line) are not escaped.
failing_case: A customer registers with the name ``. Every operator who opens the dashboard runs that script in the page that holds the refund controls. A name with an id containing `"` breaks out of data-id the same way.
remediation: Build rows with createElement and textContent, or escape every interpolated value through one helper. Add a CSP without unsafe-inline.

title: Unchecking a box never removes the order from the refund list
evidence: Only the checked branch exists. selected is a module-level array that is never cleared. renderTable (lines 26-36) rebuilds the rows unchecked on every page change and search, while selected keeps the old ids. Checking the same row twice pushes a duplicate.
failing_case: Tick order 7, untick it, tick order 9, click Refund selected. selected is [7, 9], so order 7 is refunded as well. Tick a row, go to the next page, and the id is still sent although no box shows ticked. Money goes back on orders the operator did not choose.
remediation: Keep selection as a Set keyed by id, add on check and delete on uncheck, re-apply `checked` when rows render, and clear it after a confirmed refund.

title: The Refund control is a span: no keyboard access, no role, no name for assistive technology
evidence: A span is not focusable and has no button role. app.js:49 only sets onclick, so Enter and Space do nothing even if it were focused.
failing_case: Tab through the page: focus goes search, status, checkboxes, Prev, Next, and never reaches Refund. A keyboard or screen-reader user cannot perform the page's main task (WCAG 2.1.1, level A).
remediation: Use <button type="button" id="refundBtn">Refund selected</button> and style it; keep it disabled until something is selected.

quote: 12 seats on annual billing at 20% off is $1,440 a year.
title: Pricing arithmetic is wrong: $15 x 12 seats x 12 months at 20% off is $1,728, not $1,440
evidence: 15 * 12 = 180 per month; 180 * 12 = 2,160 per year; 2,160 * 0.8 = 1,728. $1,440 matches no reading: it is 8 months of the undiscounted price, or 2,160 less 33%.
failing_case: A customer is quoted $1,440 and then invoiced $1,728, or the reverse if the seat price is meant per year ($180 x 0.8 = $144 per seat, 12 seats = $1,728 again).
remediation: Correct the figure to $1,728 (if the $15 is monthly), state the billing basis in the sentence, and keep price rules in one place the docs and code both read.

quote: **Fully accessible:** meets WCAG 2.1 AA, including 44 px touch targets (criterion 2.5.5).
title: Accessibility claim is false, and criterion 2.5.5 is level AAA, not AA
evidence: The code fails 2.1.1 (index.html:19), 2.4.7 (styles.css:19), 1.4.3 (styles.css:9, 12, 18), 1.4.1 (app.js:32) and 4.1.2 (index.html:17). Buttons are about 20 px high (styles.css:18). 2.5.5 Target Size (44 px) is AAA in WCAG 2.1, so it is not part of AA.
failing_case: An buyer or compliance reviewer relies on 'meets WCAG 2.1 AA' and ships to a regulated customer. A keyboard user cannot refund at all.
remediation: Remove the claim until an audit supports it. If kept, cite the right level (2.5.8, 24 px, is AA in WCAG 2.2) and list known gaps.

quote: **Secure:** the API key never leaves the server.
title: README says the API key stays on the server; api.js ships it to every browser
evidence: api.js:3 defines API_KEY and api.js:6 and :11 send it from client-side code loaded by index.html:25.
failing_case: A reader trusts the claim and does not rotate the key or review the deployment, while the key is public in the page source.
remediation: Fix the code first (move calls behind a server), then keep the sentence; until then delete it.

quote: Refunds are confirmed before they are sent.
title: README says refunds are confirmed first; the click handler sends them immediately
evidence: app.js:49-51 calls refund(selected) with no confirm() or dialog. index.html has no confirmation element.
failing_case: A user selects the wrong rows and clicks once. The refund request leaves with no chance to cancel.
remediation: Add the confirmation step (see the refund finding at app.js:49), or remove the sentence.

title: getOrders never checks the HTTP status, so an error body is treated as the order list
evidence: No res.ok check at api.js:6-7. app.js:41 assigns the result to orders, then app.js:11 runs `for (const o of orders)`. There is no try/catch in load().
failing_case: The API answers 401 with {"error":"unauthorized"}. orders becomes an object, `for...of` throws 'orders is not iterable', and the page keeps the old stats and rows with no message. A network failure is an unhandled rejection and the user sees nothing either.
remediation: Throw when !res.ok or when the body is not an array. In load(), catch, keep the data consistent and show an error with a retry action.

title: refund() returns ok:true without awaiting the request or reading its result
evidence: api.js:11 calls fetch without await and without a catch. Line 12 returns ok:true straight away. app.js:51 turns that into a 'Refunded N orders!' toast.
failing_case: Select two orders and click Refund while offline, or while the API answers 401 or 500. The toast says 'Refunded 2 orders!'. Nothing was refunded. A network error also becomes an unhandled promise rejection.
remediation: await the fetch, check res.ok, return the parsed result or throw. Show success only after a 2xx and show the failure with its cause otherwise. Send an idempotency key with the request.

title: Empty result shows $NaN in the AVG ORDER card
evidence: orders.length is 0 when a search matches nothing or on first load with no orders. 0 / 0 is NaN and NaN.toFixed(2) is 'NaN'. The same line also divides net revenue by all orders, including pending and refunded ones.
failing_case: Type a customer name that does not exist. The card shows '$NaN'. The table is empty with no message saying why.
remediation: Return 0 (or a dash) when there are no orders, and define the average over paid orders in the named pricing function. Add an empty-state row to the table.

title: Pagination is off by one: page 1 starts at order 11 and the first ten orders are never shown
evidence: page starts at 1 (app.js:3) but start = page * PAGE_SIZE, so page 1 slices 10..20. Prev from page 1 sets page 0, then page -1 where slice(-10, 0) returns no rows.
failing_case: Load 25 orders. The first screen shows orders 11-20. Orders 1-10 appear on no page. Clicking Prev twice shows an empty table.
remediation: Use (page - 1) * PAGE_SIZE and clamp page between 1 and the page count; disable Prev and Next at the ends.

title: Order status is shown only as a coloured 10 px dot
evidence: The span has no text and no title. styles.css:17 sets #3c3 (2.14:1 on white), #cc3 (1.71:1) and #c33 for the three states. Pending and paid are close for colour-blind users.
failing_case: A screen-reader user hears nothing in the Status column. A user with red-green colour blindness cannot tell paid from refunded. The status is the data the refund decision depends on (WCAG 1.4.1 A, 1.4.11 AA).
remediation: Print the status word in the cell (with the dot as decoration) and use colours that reach 3:1 against the background.

title: Every keystroke fires a request and responses are applied in whatever order they arrive
evidence: app.js:45 binds oninput straight to load. There is no debounce, no AbortController and no check that the response still matches the current inputs.
failing_case: Type 'ab'. The request for 'a' is slow and the request for 'ab' is fast. The 'ab' results render first, then the late 'a' response overwrites orders. The box says 'ab' while the table shows results for 'a', and the operator ticks and refunds from the wrong list.
remediation: Debounce input, abort the previous request with AbortController, and ignore any response whose request token is not the latest.

title: Refund runs on one click with no confirmation, no empty-selection guard and no double-click guard
evidence: The handler calls refund(selected) immediately. selected is not checked for length, the control is not disabled while the call is pending, and selected is not cleared afterwards (line 51).
failing_case: Click Refund selected with nothing ticked: the toast says 'Refunded 0 orders!'. Select 3 orders and double-click: two POSTs with the same ids go out, which can refund twice.
remediation: Disable the button when nothing is selected, ask for confirmation that names the count and total, disable during the call, send an idempotency key, and clear the selection only after a 2xx.

title: Focus outline removed from every button, input and select with no replacement
evidence: No :focus-visible rule exists anywhere in styles.css.
failing_case: Tab to Prev, Next, the search box or the filter: nothing on screen shows where focus is (WCAG 2.4.7 AA).
remediation: Delete the rule, or replace it with a :focus-visible outline of at least 2px and 3:1 contrast.

title: Stat card labels are 11 px #aaa on white: 2.32:1
evidence: Contrast computed for #aaa on #fff = 2.32:1, below 4.5:1 for normal text (WCAG 1.4.3 AA). The text is also 11 px.
failing_case: REVENUE, ORDERS and AVG ORDER are hard to read in daylight or for low-vision users; the number has no other label.
remediation: Use a colour of at least 4.5:1 on white (for example #595959) at 12 px or larger.

quote: .refund { border-radius: 12px; background: #8b5cf6; color: #fff; padding: 8px 12px; cursor: pointer; }
title: The primary action has white text on #8b5cf6: 4.23:1, under the 4.5:1 minimum
evidence: Contrast computed for #fff on #8b5cf6 = 4.23:1. The same colour ends the header gradient (line 3). Text is regular weight and about 16 px, so the large-text 3:1 exception does not apply.
failing_case: Low-vision users find the single destructive action harder to read than any other control (WCAG 1.4.3 AA).
remediation: Darken the background to at least 4.5:1 with white (for example #6d28d9), and give the button hover and focus-visible states.

quote: button { border: 0; background: none; color: #aaa; padding: 2px 4px; font-size: 12px; }
title: Prev and Next buttons are 12 px #aaa with no background (2.06:1) and a tiny hit area
evidence: #aaa on the #F4F1EA page background computes to 2.06:1. Padding of 2px 4px gives a target about 20 px high. The buttons have no border, so they do not read as buttons.
failing_case: On a phone, Prev and Next are hard to see and hard to hit; a user taps the wrong one or gives up paging (WCAG 1.4.3 AA; the 24 px target in 2.5.8 is WCAG 2.2 AA).
remediation: Give the buttons a visible border or fill, text at 4.5:1 or better, and a minimum 24 px (ideally 44 px) hit area.

title: Search text is put into the URL without encoding
evidence: query comes from the #q input (app.js:39) and is interpolated raw. No encodeURIComponent.
failing_case: Search for `a&status=refunded` or `R&D #1`. The & and # change or truncate the query string, so the server filters on the wrong values.
remediation: Build the URL with URLSearchParams or wrap each value in encodeURIComponent.

title: Discount, tax and revenue rules are written inside a render function
evidence: app.js:9-17 holds the gold discount (10%), the 8.25% tax and the paid/refunded sign inside renderStats, with magic numbers and no test. The table at line 32 shows the raw `o.total`, so the two views of the same order disagree. Adding 8.25% tax to 'revenue' also overstates it if totals already include tax.
failing_case: A gold customer order of 100 shows $100 in the table but contributes 97.43 to REVENUE. Changing the tax rate means editing a UI function.
remediation: Move the arithmetic into one pure, named function (for example orderNet(order)) with constants and a unit test. The view only formats the result.

title: Page count rounds down, and Next, Prev and search never bound or reset the page
evidence: Math.floor drops the last partial page. Lines 47-48 increment and decrement page with no limit. load() (line 42) does not reset page when the search changes.
failing_case: With 25 orders the label reads 'Page 1 of 2' although 3 pages exist. With 9 orders it reads 'Page 1 of 0'. On page 3, search for something that returns 4 orders: the table stays empty and the label says 'Page 3 of 0'.
remediation: Use Math.max(1, Math.ceil(n / PAGE_SIZE)), clamp page in one function, and set page = 1 on every new query.

title: Search box and status filter have no accessible name; row checkboxes and first column header are unnamed
evidence: The input uses a placeholder as its only label. <select id="status"> (line 18) has no label at all. The checkbox in app.js:32 has no label and the first <th> (index.html:21) is empty.
failing_case: A screen reader announces 'edit text' and 'combo box' with no purpose, and 'checkbox' for every row with no hint which order it selects (WCAG 1.3.1, 4.1.2).
remediation: Add <label> or aria-label to the input and select, aria-label="Select order {id}" on each checkbox, and a visually hidden header text for column one.

title: Toast is not a live region, so the refund result is never announced
evidence: No role="status" or aria-live. app.js:51 sets textContent and display:block only. The toast is never hidden again either.
failing_case: A screen-reader user clicks Refund (if they could reach it) and hears nothing. A sighted user sees the toast stay on screen until reload.
remediation: Add role="status" (and role="alert" for failures), and hide the toast after a few seconds or on dismiss.

title: Table is fixed at 1000 px wide, and the three-column card grid does not collapse
evidence: No media queries in styles.css. The .cards grid at line 6 stays at repeat(3, 1fr), and the toolbar does not wrap.
failing_case: At 390 px the table forces a sideways scroll on the whole page; at 200% zoom on a 1360 px screen the same happens (WCAG 1.4.10 reflow). Card numbers at 32 px bold are squeezed to about 100 px each.
remediation: Use width: 100% in a container with overflow-x: auto, a media query that makes .cards one column under about 640 px, and flex-wrap on .toolbar.

title: The toast pulses forever and ignores prefers-reduced-motion
evidence: @keyframes pop at line 21 scales 1 to 1.05 with iteration count infinite. No @media (prefers-reduced-motion) block exists. app.js never hides the toast, so it pulses until reload.
failing_case: After one refund, a user with a vestibular disorder gets a permanently scaling box in the corner of every view (WCAG 2.2.2 A for moving content over 5 seconds with no way to stop it; 2.3.3 AAA).
remediation: Drop the animation, or run it once and wrap it in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference). Hide the toast after a timeout.

title: Header eyebrow is 11 px pale lilac on the purple gradient: 2.5:1 to 2.64:1
failing_case: The 'DASHBOARD — OVERVIEW' line is unreadable for low-vision users. It adds nothing the h1 does not already say.
remediation: Remove the eyebrow, or use white at 12 px or larger.

quote: td:nth-child(2) { max-width: 120px; white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }
title: Long customer names are cut off at 120 px with no ellipsis and no way to read the rest
evidence: overflow: hidden with no text-overflow and no title attribute in app.js:32.
failing_case: 'Alexandria Montgomery-Fitzgerald' shows as 'Alexandria Montgomery-Fi' with no hint that text is missing; two customers with the same first 120 px look identical on a refund list.
remediation: Add text-overflow: ellipsis and a title with the full name, or let the cell wrap.
